answer_raw:
For the fastest performance, you would rent a **GPU Droplet** at **$2.50/hr** as of March 2026 [3].

For a 7B model, the cheapest option that would run it at all is likely the **$24/mo** Agent Droplet (2 vCPU, 4 GiB RAM) as of October 2026 [2].

## Speed vs. Feasibility

**The Fastest Option**
If you want the highest throughput for LLM inference, the **GPU Droplets** are the top tier, priced at **$2.50/hr** as of March 2026 [3]. While standard droplets use CPUs, these specialized nodes are designed for the compute-heavy requirements of transformer-based models.

**The Cheapest "Run-at-all" Option**
Running a 7B model on a standard CPU-based droplet is a struggle because of RAM constraints. A 7B model typically requires roughly 4GB to 8GB of RAM depending on the quantization (e.g., 4-bit vs 8-bit) [8].

*   **The $4/mo Basic Droplet** (512 MiB RAM) as of undated source [7] will not run a 7B model; it will crash immediately due to Out-of-Memory (OOM) errors.
*   **The $24/mo Agent Droplet** (4 GiB RAM) as of October 2026 [2] is the most realistic "budget" entry point. You would need to use heavy 4-bit quantization (like GGUF/llama.cpp) to fit the model into that 4GB of available memory [8].

| Tier | Specs | Monthly Price | Use Case |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **GPU Droplet** | GPU-accelerated | **$2.50/hr** (as of March 2026) [3] | High-speed inference/training |
| **Agent Droplet** | 2 vCPU, 4 GiB RAM | **$24/mo** (as of Oct 2026) [2] | Minimum viable for quantized 7B |
| **Basic Droplet** | 512 MiB RAM | **$4/mo** (as of undated) [7] | Non-viable for LLMs |
